hunks.baseline: That was why we had no choice but to accept, however painfully, the tragic news of our close companions’ deaths.
hunks.sol: That was why we had no choice but to accept, however painfully, the news that our close companions had died.

hunks.baseline: The reality right in front of us was simply too horrific to give in to our emotions.
hunks.sol: The reality before us was too horrific to let ourselves be swept away by emotion.

hunks.baseline: “That concludes the briefing.”
hunks.sol: “…That concludes the meeting.”

hunks.baseline: The lights came on with the presenter’s exhausted voice, but the heavy silence pressing down on the room didn’t disperse so easily.
hunks.sol: The lights came on as the presenter finished speaking, exhaustion in his voice. But the heavy silence pressing down on the room didn’t lift.

hunks.baseline: It was a simple remark, but no one failed to understand what lay beneath it.
hunks.sol: It was a simple remark, but everyone understood what he meant.

hunks.baseline: Anyone that oblivious wouldn’t have been allowed in this room in the first place.
hunks.sol: Anyone who couldn’t read the room that well wouldn’t have been here in the first place.

hunks.baseline: The conference room had at last emptied out. A middle-aged man walked over to the coffee machine tucked in one corner and glanced at me.
hunks.sol: Once the conference room had mostly emptied, a middle-aged man walked over to the coffee machine in one corner and glanced at me.

hunks.baseline: His hair was greasy and disheveled, and dark circles ringed his eyes.
hunks.sol: His hair was greasy and disheveled, and dark circles ringed his eyes. He looked like an office worker worn down by exhaustion. I shook my head.

hunks.baseline: He looked like an office worker worn down to the bone by exhaustion. I shook my head at his offer.
Even that was only a forced smile that appeared for a moment before vanishing without a trace.
hunks.sol: Even that was a forced smile. It appeared for a moment, then vanished without a trace.

hunks.baseline: *Of course it was.*
hunks.sol: *Of course it did.*

hunks.baseline: My eyes drifted to the hologram still hanging in the air—the catastrophic casualty figures enough to rob even a thoroughly jaded politician of a smile.
hunks.sol: My eyes drifted to the hologram still hanging in the air. Its catastrophic figures were enough to wipe the smile from even a thoroughly jaded politician’s face.

hunks.baseline: “The first time I received a report about it at the White House, I thought, ‘Is this a dream?’”
hunks.sol: “When I first received the report at the White House, I thought, *Is this a dream?*”

hunks.baseline: He downed a coffee heavily laced with potions and continued.
hunks.sol: He downed a cup of coffee heavily laced with potion and continued.

hunks.baseline: “To be honest, I still think the same thing. I keep hoping all of this is one goddamn nightmare.”
hunks.sol: “To be honest, I still think that sometimes. I keep hoping all of this is one goddamn nightmare.”

hunks.baseline: But this was reality. The numbers in the reports hadn’t leveled off; they’d climbed higher with every passing day.
hunks.sol: But it was real. The figures in the reports hadn’t leveled off; they’d climbed higher every day.

hunks.baseline: Property damage in the tens of quadrillions. Tens of millions dead or injured, and even more refugees. The whole world was in a panic.
hunks.sol: Property damage measured in the tens of quadrillions. Tens of millions dead or injured, and even more people displaced. The whole world was in a panic.

hunks.baseline: “That’s why I had to announce as soon as possible that you’d returned.”
hunks.sol: “That’s why we had to announce your return as quickly as possible.”

hunks.baseline: The UN Security Council, led by its permanent members, had immediately issued an emergency statement. News of my return spread around the world after I’d gone missing in the Middle East.
hunks.sol: The UN Security Council, led by its permanent members, had immediately issued an emergency statement. News that I’d returned after going missing in the Middle East spread around the world before I’d even arrived here at the Pentagon.

hunks.baseline: Before I, the person at the center of it all, had even arrived here at the Pentagon.

preferred glossary term appears in BASE but not SOL for this hunk

hunks.baseline: “Some people thought announcing it during the discussions was premature. But given the circumstances, we had no choice. What if we made the wrong call—”
hunks.sol: “Some people thought it was too soon to make the announcement while we were still discussing it. But given the circumstances, we had no choice. If we made the wrong call—”

hunks.baseline: Because it was too late to put the genie back in the bottle now?
hunks.sol: Because it was too late to take the announcement back?

hunks.baseline: But if the news of my return hadn’t gotten out, people would have been swept into an even more uncontrollable maelstrom.
hunks.sol: But if word of my return hadn’t gotten out, people would have been swept into an even worse spiral.

hunks.baseline: And the seed of that disaster had already blossomed.
All because of an unprecedented monster: Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.
hunks.sol: And the seed of that disaster had already blossomed, thanks to an unprecedented monster: Black Dragon Duke Morgoth.

hunks.baseline: “Jin, I’ve handled countless major crises over the past twelve years as President of the United States. But there’s always been one matter that came before all the others—the most important priority.”
hunks.sol: “Jin, I’ve dealt with countless matters of national importance in my twelve years as President of the United States. But one issue has always come before all the others.”

hunks.baseline: Ever since Demon King Asmodeus descended upon this world, every country had been facing the same problem.
hunks.sol: Ever since Demon King Asmodeus descended upon this world, every country had faced the same problem.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. The Gates that remained after the Great Cataclysm, and the preparations for a possible second Great Cataclysm—they were our top priorities.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. Dealing with the Gates that remained after the Great Cataclysm—and preparing for the possibility of a second one—have been our highest priorities.”

hunks.baseline: He stared silently down at his empty coffee cup, then added weakly, “And our preparations failed. Or, more precisely…”
hunks.sol: He stared silently at his empty coffee cup, then added weakly, “And those preparations failed. Or, more precisely…”

hunks.baseline: “Something showed up that was too strong for us to handle, even though we were preparing for it. I understand.”
hunks.sol: “Something appeared that was too strong for us to handle, even though we’d prepared for it. I understand.”

hunks.baseline: Even if the footage didn’t show all of his strength, what I’d seen onscreen was beyond anything any named monster had displayed from the Great Cataclysm up to now.
hunks.sol: Even if what I’d seen on the video wasn’t the full extent of his strength, no named monster that had appeared since the Great Cataclysm could compare to him.

hunks.baseline: There was only one being who could compare.
hunks.sol: Except one.

hunks.baseline: No one but the absolute evil known as the Demon King Asmodeus—the one called not merely a calamity, but the end of the world.
hunks.sol: Demon King Asmodeus, the absolute evil called not merely a calamity, but the end of the world.

hunks.baseline: “But your preparations couldn’t be complete without *him* there, could they?”
hunks.sol: “But those preparations could only be complete with *him*, couldn’t they?”

hunks.baseline: If two atomic bombs had brought World War II to an end, Cheon Taemin had saved all of humanity by weathering the Great Cataclysm with his own body.
hunks.sol: If two atomic bombs had brought World War II to an end, Cheon Taemin had saved all of humanity by fighting his way through the Great Cataclysm.

hunks.baseline: “But Sky’s absence isn’t our only problem. Morgoth’s power is a calamity all on its own…but he has something no other monster can compare to.”
hunks.sol: “But Sky’s absence isn’t our only problem. Morgoth’s power is a calamity in itself…but there’s something about him that sets him apart from every other monster.”

hunks.baseline: “I’ve dealt with monsters enough to be sick of them.”
hunks.sol: “I’ve dealt with enough monsters to be sick of them.”

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t remember every meal I’d eaten in my life. In the same way, I’d taken down too many monsters to count, going all the way back to my days as an F-rank Hunter.
hunks.sol: Just as I couldn’t count every meal I’d eaten in my life, I couldn’t count the monsters I’d brought down since my days as an F-rank Hunter.

hunks.baseline: No matter how intelligent they were, no matter how strong they were, monsters were born with an instinct to kill.
hunks.sol: Regardless of how intelligent or powerful they were, monsters were born with an instinct to kill.

hunks.baseline: *If anything, the stronger they were, the more they wanted to crush everything beneath them. They tried to solve everything with overwhelming force.*
hunks.sol: *If anything, the stronger they were, the more they wanted to crush everything beneath them. They tried to settle everything with overwhelming force.*

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King, who wasn’t here, was one. And the Doppelganger, who had helped set Morgoth’s summoning in motion, had long ago infiltrated human society and operated in secret.
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King, who wasn’t here, was one. The Doppelganger whose actions had led to Morgoth’s summoning had even infiltrated human society long ago and worked in secret.

hunks.baseline: He wasn’t just bluffing or tricking people. He offered surrender in earnest, and if they accepted, he guaranteed their survival.
hunks.sol: He wasn’t merely bluffing or trying to deceive anyone. He offered surrender in earnest, and if people accepted, he guaranteed their survival.

hunks.baseline: His actions had caused more division than ever before.
hunks.sol: And that had caused greater division than ever.

hunks.baseline: “Twenty-three countries have already surrendered to Morgoth. Besides the Arab League, which suffered the heaviest losses, some major South American countries have given up resisting.”
hunks.sol: “Twenty-three countries have already surrendered to Morgoth. Along with the Arab League, which suffered the heaviest losses, several major South American countries have given up resisting.”

hunks.baseline: “The Moscow incident had a huge impact. We did everything we could to contain it, but we couldn’t stop the information from spreading.”
hunks.sol: “What happened in Moscow had a huge impact. We tried to control the situation, but we couldn’t stop the news from spreading.”

hunks.baseline: Faced with the most powerful desire of all—survival—people were crumbling one after another.
hunks.sol: Faced with the most powerful desire of all—the will to survive—people were crumbling one after another.

hunks.baseline: “A similar thing happened early in the Great Cataclysm, but this is different. Everyone’s shaken.”
hunks.sol: “Something similar happened early in the Great Cataclysm, but this is different. Everyone’s shaken.”

hunks.baseline: The reason humanity had managed to bring the Great Cataclysm to an end with a victory was simpler than you might think.
hunks.sol: The reason humanity had managed to win the Great Cataclysm was simpler than you might think.

hunks.baseline: He burned down cities and overturned mountains and seas.
hunks.sol: He burned cities and overturned mountains and seas.

hunks.baseline: To him, it was as if a cockroach found in his house one day had sworn to obey him in exchange for living together.
hunks.sol: To him, that would have been like a cockroach he’d found in his house one day pledging obedience in exchange for living there alongside him.

hunks.baseline: That was how humanity had been able to fight back with all its strength, united in purpose.
hunks.sol: And so humanity had fought back with all its strength, united in purpose.

hunks.baseline: Fortunately, they had Cheon Taemin, a savior, and no other choice.
hunks.sol: Fortunately, they’d had a savior in Cheon Taemin. They’d had no other choice.

hunks.baseline: He took human form and followed human customs.
hunks.sol: He took human form and followed human ways.

hunks.baseline: For those who resisted, he offered devastating destruction and death. For those who surrendered, he guaranteed survival.
hunks.sol: Those who resisted faced devastating destruction and death. Those who surrendered were guaranteed survival.

hunks.baseline: “If you hadn’t appeared in time, I might be signing the goddamn surrender documents by now.”
hunks.sol: “If you hadn’t appeared when you did, I might be signing a goddamn surrender document right now.”

hunks.baseline: President Doramp gave a bitter smile, but I couldn’t smile. My thoughts were tearing through my head.
hunks.sol: President Doramp smiled bitterly, but I couldn’t smile. My thoughts were racing.

hunks.baseline: *I came in time? Me?*
hunks.sol: *I appeared in time? Me?*

hunks.baseline: Blood drops fell, one after another. It was running from between my fingers where I’d clenched my fist without realizing it. After a brief silence, President Doramp spoke.
hunks.sol: Drops of blood struck the floor. I’d clenched my fist without realizing it, and blood was running between my fingers. After a brief silence, President Doramp spoke.

hunks.baseline: “Jin, what’s done is done. And nobody blames you. Unlike you, we were all in our own places, and we still couldn’t stop Morgoth.”
hunks.sol: “Jin, it’s already happened. And nobody blames you. While you were gone, the rest of us were at our posts, and we still couldn’t stop Morgoth.”

hunks.baseline: Ever since I’d gained powers unlike anyone else’s, I’d struggled at every turn. And as a result, I’d saved countless lives.
hunks.sol: Ever since I’d gained powers unlike anyone else’s, I’d struggled at every turn. I’d saved countless lives because of it.

hunks.baseline: But the sudden surges of anger and self-blame still refused to fade.
hunks.sol: But that didn’t make the sudden surges of anger and self-blame any easier to shake.

hunks.baseline: *They probably won’t, even after everything is over.*
hunks.sol: *They probably won’t go away even after this is over.*

hunks.baseline: People called me the savior of a new age, but I was only human, just like them.
hunks.sol: People called me the savior of a new age, but I was human, just like them.

hunks.baseline: An aide rushed into the conference room. Behind him were several familiar faces.
hunks.sol: An aide rushed into the conference room. Behind him, I saw familiar faces.

hunks.baseline: Every one of them wore a tight expression, their eyes downcast.
hunks.sol: Every mouth was set, every gaze somber.

hunks.baseline: The air froze in an instant. At the aide’s touch, a holographic video sprang into the air.
hunks.sol: The air seemed to freeze. At the aide’s touch, a holographic video sprang into the air.

hunks.baseline: *Pop.*
hunks.sol: *Flash.*

hunks.baseline: Through the constant crackle of static, a landscape tens of thousands of kilometers away filled the vast conference room.
hunks.sol: Through the constant crackle of static, a scene from tens of thousands of kilometers away filled the vast conference room.

hunks.baseline: A Dragon Lair rose over the blackened earth once known as Moscow, blocking everyone’s view.
hunks.sol: A Dragon Lair towered over the blackened earth once known as Moscow, filling everyone’s field of view.
